summary: A guide to fine-tuning the AAPS Profile (basal, ISF, I:C) once the basic setup and objectives are done: how to test with closed loop and without automations or sensitivity features, which IOB and BG patterns point to which Profile change, and how to measure the I:C ratio. Not medical advice. "Profile" is the app's term for the basal/ISF/IC/target settings; ISF, IOB, COB, BG and SMB are the app's abbreviations.

sections.summary: Page introduction and medical disclaimer: what the guide covers and why closed loop helps with basal testing.

sections.heading: Changing profile's settings, how to proceed
sections.summary: The method: observe BG and IOB over several days, find repeating patterns, change one Profile value at a time in small steps.

sections.heading: Recommended settings and advice while tweaking basal
sections.summary: Test conditions: closed loop on, automations and DynISF/AutoISF/Autosens off, no manual actions, which additional graphs to show, and what to avoid during testing.

sections.summary: Which values make a Profile too strong.

sections.heading: IOB Observations
sections.summary: Heading for IOB patterns; IOB over several days can be seen in Nightscout reports.

sections.heading: IOB positive
sections.summary: Constantly positive IOB suggests the Profile basal is too weak.

sections.heading: IOB negative
sections.summary: Constantly negative IOB suggests basal too strong, past exercise, or a previous oversized bolus.

sections.heading: BG Target Observations
sections.summary: Heading for patterns around the BG target.

sections.heading: Stuck High
sections.summary: Causes of BG staying high: ISF too weak, basal too weak, a safety limit such as MaxIOB (check the SMB tab), or site problems.

sections.heading: Stuck Low
sections.summary: Causes of BG staying low: ISF or basal too strong.

sections.heading: Rollercoaster (ups and downs)
sections.summary: Ups and downs may mean the ISF is too strong.

sections.heading: Fast rise and BG going high
sections.summary: Fast carbs, pre-bolus timing or a too weak bolus after meals.

sections.heading: Fast rise and then BG going low
sections.summary: A too aggressive Profile or bolus after meals; consider a pre-bolus.

sections.heading: [How to calculate your I:C](#your-aaps-profile-insulin-to-carbs-ratio)
sections.summary: Measuring the insulin-to-carbs ratio from a test meal: record insulin and IOB before and after, subtract basal, divide.
